From: Matt Dawson <matt.dawson@signalhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 21:47:12 -0500
Subject: Re: load-run: repeated stalls on multiplexed connections

Hannah —

We ran the agreed 400-concurrent-stream load test this evening (local repro script attached). Around minute 12 we started seeing repeated silent windows where the client receives the last chunk and then the socket remains open with no further chunks for ~10–30s until the client-side timeout kicks in. From our side we see a mix of 503s and a lot of WS 101->1006 transitions. Throughput drops by ~60% for affected streams.

Attached: signalhealth-client-logs-20261219.tar.gz (gzip), pcap sample.

We also uploaded a short curl reproducer to the Drive link below. This is blocking our go/no-go for production rollout next week — need a clear mitigation path ASAP.

Matt
Product Eng, SignalHealth
--

Subject: Re: load-run: repeated stalls on multiplexed connections

Quick triage notes after an initial pass on the uploaded traces:
- I pulled the trace for one of the stalled streams: trace_id=9b7f2c4a-ef3a-4d2b-8e1f-11f0c2d5a7ab. Token emission from the model appears continuous on the worker, but there is a long gap between chunk flushes at the proxy layer (~12s).
- The worker's send buffer shows steady writes; the proxy (edge-router-03) is observing backpressure and is occasionally coalescing small writes into larger TCP frames. That coalescing plus an intermittent epoll wakeup delay looks like a head-of-line blocking issue under high multiplexing.
- Additional observation: there is an increase in 5xx error rates when TCP window scaling interacts poorly with our Nginx-based edge on the client's IP range.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Short-term: enforce per-connection concurrency cap on the customer's routing policy (reduce to 8 streams/conn). This is config only and safe to apply per-tenant.
2) Medium-term: enable chunked-flush-more-frequently flag on the affected edge pool for this tenant (should reduce coalescing but may increase token-plan cost).
3) Long-term: change edge epoll tuning and bump net.core.netdev_max_backlog on the proxies; requires rollout and kernel tuning.

I'll prepare an infra playbook. Dev — can you validate whether enabling more aggressive flushes will impact our CPU/latency SLOs?

Jonas
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary: SignalHealth multiplexed-stream stalls — action required

Markus —

Summary: SignalHealth hit a production-representative load test where multiplexed clients (20 streams per conn) experienced repeated multi-second silent windows on streaming responses. Workers continue to generate tokens; the pause appears at the proxy/edge flush layer (coalescing + epoll wake delays) leading to client-visible stalls and increased 5xx counts. Impact: severe throughput degradation for the tenant and an immediate blocker for their rollout next week.

Immediate actions taken:
- SRE (Jonas) recommends per-tenant per-conn concurrency cap (<=8 streams/conn) and a targeted flag to increase chunked flush frequency for the customer's edge pool. Config-only mitigations ready for apply and fast rollback.
- Runtime (Dev) to validate CPU/latency delta for more aggressive flushes; initial estimate: ~8–12% token CPU overhead at peak.
- Customer can reproduce and has provided artifacts (logs + pcap).

Ask: please approve the outbound-config mitigation (per-tenant cap + flush flag) as an emergency customer-facing change. We'll prepare a postmortem and longer-term infra plan (epoll tuning & edge rollout) to prevent recurrence.

I can join a quick phone/war-room with you and Jonas at 09:30 ET to walk through the artifacts if helpful.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
